-
- जन्म लेता है ।
व्याख्या——प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकान्' – जो लोग | उद्देश्य भोग भोगनेका नहीं है, प्रत्युत परमात्मप्राप्तिका है,
वह योगभ्रष्ट किसी सूक्ष्म वासनाके कारण स्वर्गमें चला
जाय, तो वहाँ उसकी साधन-सम्पत्ति क्षीण नहीं होती ।
इसलिये वह वहाँ असीम वर्षोंतक रहता है अर्थात् उसके
लिये वहाँ रहनेकी कोई सीमा नहीं होती।
शास्त्रीय विधि-विधानसे यज्ञ आदि कर्मोंको सांगोपांग
करते हैं, उन लोगोंका स्वर्गादि लोकोंपर अधिकार है,
इसलिये उन लोकोंको यहाँ 'पुण्यकर्म करनेवालोंके लोक'
कहा गया है। तात्पर्य है कि उन लोकोंमें पुण्यकर्म
करनेवाले ही जाते हैं, पापकर्म करनेवाले नहीं । परन्तु जिन
साधकोंको पुण्य-कर्मोंके फलरूप सुख भोगनेकी इच्छा
नहीं है, उनको वे स्वर्गादि लोक विघ्नरूपमें और मुफ्तमें
मिलते हैं ! तात्पर्य है कि यज्ञादि शुभ कर्म करनेवालोंको
परिश्रम करना पड़ता है, उन लोकोंकी याचना - प्रार्थना
करनी पड़ती है, यज्ञादि कर्मोंको विधि-विधान से और
सांगोपांग करना पड़ता है, तब कहीं उनको स्वर्गादि
लोकोंकी प्राप्ति होती है । वहाँ भी उनकी भोगोंकी वासना
बनी रहती है; क्योंकि उनका उद्देश्य ही भोग भोगनेका
था । परन्तु जो किसी कारणवश अन्तसमयमें साधनसे
विचलितमना हो जाते हैं, उनको स्वर्गादि लोकोंकी प्राप्तिके
लिये न तो परिश्रम करना पड़ता है, न उनकी याचना करनी
पड़ती है और न उनकी प्राप्तिके लिये यज्ञादि शुभ कर्म
ही करने पड़ते हैं । फिर भी उनको स्वर्गादि लोकोंकी
प्राप्ति हो जाती है। वहाँ रहनेपर भी उनकी वहाँके भोगोंसे
अरुचि हो जाती है; क्योंकि उनका उद्देश्य भोग भोगनेका
था ही नहीं। वे तो केवल सांसारिक सूक्ष्म वासनाके कारण
उन लोकोंमें जाते हैं। परन्तु उनकी वह वासना भोगी
पुरुषोंकी वासनाके समान नहीं होती ।
जो केवल भोग भोगनेके लिये स्वर्गमें जाते हैं, वे जैसे
भोगोंमें तल्लीन होते हैं, वैसे योगभ्रष्ट तल्लीन नहीं हो
सकता। कारण कि भोगोंकी इच्छावाले पुरुष भोगबुद्धिसे
भोगोंको स्वीकार करते हैं और योगभ्रष्टको विघ्नरूपसे
भोगोंमें जाना पड़ता है।
,
,
जो भोग भोगनेके उद्देश्यसे ऊँचे लोकोंमें जाते हैं,
उनका उन लोकोंमें जाना कर्मजन्य है । परन्तु योगभ्रष्टका
ऊँचे लोकोंमें जाना कर्मजन्य नहीं है; किन्तु यह तो योगका
प्रभाव है, उनकी साधन-सम्पत्तिका प्रभाव है, उनके सत्-
उद्देश्यका प्रभाव है।
स्वर्ग आदिका सुख भोगनेके उद्देश्यसे जो उन
लोकोंमें जाते हैं, उनको न तो वहाँ रहनेमें स्वतन्त्रता है और
न वहाँसे आनेमें ही स्वतन्त्रता है । उन्होंने भोग भोगनेके
उद्देश्यसे ही यज्ञादि कर्म किये हैं, इसलिये उन शुभ
कर्मोंका फल जबतक समाप्त नहीं होता, तबतक वे
वहाँसे नीचे नहीं आ सकते और शुभ कर्मोंका फल
समाप्त होनेपर वे वहाँ रह भी नहीं सकते । परन्तु जो
परमात्माकी प्राप्तिके लिये ही साधन करनेवाले हैं और
केवल अन्तसमयमें योगसे विचलित होनेके कारण स्वर्ग
आदिमें गये हैं, उनका वासनाके तारतम्यके कारण वहाँ
ज्यादा - कम रहना हो सकता है, पर वे वहाँके भोगोंमें फँस
नहीं सकते। कारण कि जब योगका जिज्ञासु भी
शब्दब्रह्मका अतिक्रमण कर जाता है (छठे अध्यायका
चौवालीसवाँ श्लोक), तब वह योगभ्रष्ट वहाँ फँस ही कैसे
सकता है ?
-
'शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते' – स्वर्गादि
लोकोंके भोग भोगनेपर जब भोगोंसे अरुचि हो जाती है,
तब वह योगभ्रष्ट लौटकर मृत्युलोकमें आता है और शुद्ध
श्रीमानोंके घरमें जन्म लेता है । उसके फिर लौटकर आनेमें
क्या कारण है ? वास्तवमें इसका कारण तो भगवान् ही
जानें; किन्तु गीतापर विचार करनेसे ऐसा दीखता है कि
वह मनुष्य - जन्ममें साधन करता रहा । वह साधनको छोड़ना
नहीं चाहता था, पर अन्तसमयमें साधन छूट गया। अतः
उस साधनका जो महत्त्व उसके अन्तःकरणमें अंकित है,
'उषित्वा शाश्वतीः समाः ' — स्वर्गादि ऊँचे लोकोंमें
यज्ञादि शुभकर्म करनेवाले भी ( भोग भोगनेके उद्देश्यसे)
जाते हैं और योगभ्रष्ट भी जाते हैं । भोग भोगनेके उद्देश्यसे
स्वर्गमें जानेवालोंके पुण्य क्षीण होते हैं और पुण्योंके क्षीण
होनेपर उन्हें लौटकर मृत्युलोकमें आना पड़ता है । इसलिये
वे वहाँ सीमित वर्षोंतक ही रह सकते हैं । परन्तु जिसका | वह स्वर्गादि लोकोंमें भी उस योगभ्रष्टको अज्ञातरूपसे
english:
Shloka 41

The one who has been separated from yoga (yogabhrashta) 
acquires (prapti) the elixir of the sadhakas (sadhak-sanjivani) 
and, having acquired it, he resides in the homes of the pure (shuchiinam) 
eternal ones (shashvati) 
in the company of those who do great deeds (bahut karnevale samah) 
for a long time (ushitva) 
in the homes of the pure and noble ones (shrimateam ghe) 
and, having resided there, he is reborn (abhi jayate) 
in the worlds of those who have done good deeds (punya-kritam lokan) 
- he is born again.

Explanation: 
- The one who has been separated from yoga, who has not acquired the goal of attaining the ultimate reality, 
but has been driven to the celestial realm by a subtle desire, 
does not lose his spiritual wealth (sadhana-sampatti) there. 
Therefore, he resides there for an infinite number of years, 
i.e., there is no limit to his stay there. 
Those who perform rituals and other sacred acts according to the scriptures, 
have a right to the celestial realm and other higher worlds, 
hence they are called the 'worlds of those who have done good deeds'. 
The meaning is that only those who have done good deeds go to those worlds, 
not those who have done evil deeds. 
However, those sadhakas who do not have a desire to enjoy the fruits of their good deeds, 
are driven to the celestial realm and other higher worlds as obstacles, 
and they are given to them freely. 
The meaning is that those who perform good deeds have to exert themselves, 
have to make prayers and supplications, 
have to perform rituals and other sacred acts according to the scriptures, 
only then do they attain the celestial realm and other higher worlds. 
Even there, their desire for enjoyment remains, 
because their ultimate goal was to enjoy the fruits of their good deeds. 
But those who are separated from yoga, 
who are driven to the celestial realm and other higher worlds by a subtle desire, 
do not have to exert themselves, 
do not have to make prayers and supplications, 
and do not have to perform rituals and other sacred acts according to the scriptures, 
and yet they attain the celestial realm and other higher worlds. 
Even there, their desire for enjoyment is satiated, 
because their ultimate goal was not to enjoy the fruits of their good deeds. 
They are driven to the celestial realm and other higher worlds by a subtle desire, 
but their desire is not the same as that of those who are driven by a desire to enjoy the fruits of their good deeds. 
Those who are driven by a desire to enjoy the fruits of their good deeds, 
are completely absorbed in the enjoyment of those fruits, 
just as the yogabhrashta is not completely absorbed in the enjoyment of those fruits. 
The reason is that those who are driven by a desire to enjoy the fruits of their good deeds, 
accept those fruits with a sense of attachment, 
while the yogabhrashta is driven to the celestial realm and other higher worlds as an obstacle, 
and therefore he cannot be completely absorbed in the enjoyment of those fruits.

Shloka 41 (continued)

The yogabhrashta is reborn in the homes of the pure and noble ones (shrimateam ghe) 
after he has lost his taste for the enjoyment of the celestial realm and other higher worlds. 
What is the reason for his return to the mortal world? 
In reality, only the Lord knows this. 
However, it appears from the Gita that he was a sadhaka in his previous birth. 
He did not want to give up his sadhana, 
but in the end, he lost his grip on it. 
Therefore, the value of his sadhana, which was imprinted in his heart, 
is the reason for his return to the mortal world.

Shloka 42

Even the yogabhrashta is born in the homes of the pure and noble ones (shrimateam ghe) 
after he has lost his taste for the enjoyment of the celestial realm and other higher worlds. 
The yogabhrashta is also born in the celestial realm and other higher worlds, 
just like those who perform good deeds (punya-kritam lokan) 
are born there. 
The good deeds of those who are driven to the celestial realm and other higher worlds 
by a desire to enjoy the fruits of their good deeds, 
are exhausted, 
and when their good deeds are exhausted, 
they have to return to the mortal world. 
Therefore, they can only stay in the celestial realm and other higher worlds for a limited period. 
But the yogabhrashta, who is driven to the celestial realm and other higher worlds 
by a subtle desire, 
can stay there for an infinite number of years, 
because his subtle desire is not known to anyone. 
The yogabhrashta is driven to the celestial realm and other higher worlds 
by a subtle desire, 
but his subtle desire is not the same as that of those who are driven by a desire to enjoy the fruits of their good deeds. 
Those who are driven by a desire to enjoy the fruits of their good deeds, 
are completely absorbed in the enjoyment of those fruits, 
just as the yogabhrashta is not completely absorbed in the enjoyment of those fruits. 
The reason is that those who are driven by a desire to enjoy the fruits of their good deeds, 
accept those fruits with a sense of attachment, 
while the yogabhrashta is driven to the celestial realm and other higher worlds as an obstacle, 
and therefore he cannot be completely absorbed in the enjoyment of those fruits.
